analysis.investment_thesis: Cyient is the closest to a Magic Formula candidate in this batch: earnings yield of ~11.3% (EBIT 1,138 Cr / EV ~10,071 Cr) is approaching attractive territory, and ROIC on tangible capital is decent at ~22%. However, the FY2025 margin contraction — operating income fell from 1,303 to 1,138 Cr despite revenue growth — is exactly the kind of earnings quality deterioration that makes me wait rather than act.
key_strengths: Earnings yield of ~11.3% (EV = 10,071 Cr on EBIT of 1,138 Cr) is the best in this peer group, approaching the >12% threshold
Virtually debt-free in practice (net cash position: cash 1,067 Cr vs debt 513 Cr) reduces financial risk significantly
9-year revenue CAGR of 10.1% shows consistent top-line compounding across aerospace, defense, utilities, and digital services
key_risks: Operating income declined from 1,303 Cr (FY24) to 1,138 Cr (FY25) — a 13% drop — while revenue grew, signaling margin pressure from wage inflation or mix shift
Net profit also declined from 703 to 648 Cr (FY24→FY25) — two consecutive metrics moving the wrong direction kills conviction
ROCE of 16.6% is below my 20% threshold; the large equity base (5,565 Cr) from acquisitions dilutes capital efficiency
red_flags: Finance costs surged from 16 Cr (FY16) to 93-116 Cr (FY24-25), a 21.6% CAGR — acquisitions have added meaningful debt servicing burden
Other income collapsed from consistently 100-160 Cr range to negative 2 Cr in FY24 before partial recovery — suggests non-recurring items were masking core earnings weakness
analysis.detailed_analysis: EV calculation: Market Cap 10,625 + Debt 513 - Cash 1,067 = 10,071 Cr. EBIT (Operating Income) FY25 = 1,138 Cr → Earnings Yield = 11.3%. Invested capital (equity 5,565 + debt 513 - cash 1,067) = ~5,011 Cr → ROIC = 22.7%. These numbers look decent, but the FY2025 earnings regression is a yellow flag. The Magic Formula works best when high ROIC is durable — one bad year can be ignored, but the trend here (EBIT peak 1,303 Cr in FY24, now 1,138) warrants monitoring. At current levels, Cyient is a Hold with potential to become a Buy if margins stabilize and earnings yield crosses 13%+.
